nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سُورَةٌ أَنزَلْنَاهَا وَفَرَضْنَاهَا﴾.
That is, this is a sura.
 Al-Aʿraj, Mujāhid, Qatāda and Abū ʿAmr read ﴿وفَرَّضْنَاهَا﴾ [with a doubled rāʾ].
 Qatāda said: That is, We made it clear.
 And Abū ʿAmr said: That is, We set it out in detail.
 The meaning of ﴿فَرَضْنَاهَا﴾ is: We prescribed the legal punishments (الحدود) that are in it, that is, We made them obligatory, by making them a duty (فرض).

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌٌ﴾.
 There is an omission in the statement.
 The meaning is: Were it not for the favour of Allah upon you and His mercy, a great punishment would have befallen the liar among you.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُوا بِٱلإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِّنْكُمْْ﴾.
 Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are those who said about ʿĀʾisha what they said.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: A lie is called إفك; its origin is from their saying أَفَكَهُ يأْفِكُهُ when he turns him away from something; so a lie was called إفك because it is turned away from the truth and inverted from it; and from it comes المؤتفكات (the overturned cities).
Those who came with the slander (الإِفك) were — according to what has been related — "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy", "Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha" and "Ḥassān ibn Thābit".
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرّاً لَّكُمْ بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
The address is to ʿĀʾisha, her family and Ṣafwān.
That is, you are rewarded for it, and the Qurʾān came down concerning them.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُ مِنْهُمْ لَهُ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.
 Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿ٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُ﴾ is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl.
 And al-Zuhrī related from ʿUrwa from ʿĀʾisha that she said: He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy.
 Ḥumayd ibn Qays and Yaʿqūb read ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلَّى كُبْرَهُ﴾ with ḍamma on the kāf; Yaʿqūb said: as you say "the one who undertook the bulk of it (عُظْمه)".
 Al-Farrāʾ said: It is a good option in grammar.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The leading grammarians disagreed with him on that; Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ was asked: "Do you read ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلَّى كُبْرَهُ﴾?" He said: "No; الكُبْر is only in lineage."
 Abū Jaʿfar said: He means that one says: "the eldest (الكُبْر) of so-and-so's children belongs to so-and-so."

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّوْلاۤ إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً﴾.
That is: why did the believing men and believing women not think well of themselves?
That is, of the people of their religion and those who stand in their place.
 And the meaning of His saying ﴿أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ﴾ is: you plunged into it.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, some of you relate it from others.
 ʿĀʾisha and Ibn Yaʿmar read: ﴿إِذْ تلِقُوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ﴾ with kasra on the lām and ḍamma on the qāf; one says وَلَق، يَلِقُ when someone hastens in lying and the like.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُواْ لِمِثْلِهِ أَبَداً﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, He forbids you.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةُ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
 Saʿīd related from Qatāda that he said: That zinā should become public.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجْلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا مِئَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no disagreement among the exegetes that this abrogates His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَاللاَّتِي يَأْتِينَ الفَاحِشَةَ مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse, and His saying ﴿وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا﴾.
So whoever of the women committed adultery was confined until she died, and whoever of the men committed adultery was harmed.
 Mujāhid said: [Harmed] by reviling; then that was abrogated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجْلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا مِئَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾.
 They differed about the meaning:
Most of the exegetes said: This is general in wording but specific in what is intended.
 The meaning is: the fornicatress and the fornicator among the unmarried — flog each one of them a hundred lashes.
 And some of them said: It is general, covering everyone who commits zinā, whether unmarried or muḥṣan (married); he argued by the ḥadīth of ʿUbāda and by the ḥadīth of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he flogged Shurāḥa on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and said: "I flogged her by the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and stoned her by the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
 Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, in suspending the legal punishments.
 The meaning according to their view is: do not take pity on them and so abandon their punishment when they commit zinā.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
 It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: الطائفة is one man and upwards.
 And Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid that he said: الطائفة is one man and more.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī said likewise.
 And Ibn ʿUyayna related from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from ʿAṭāʾ that he said: الطائفة is two men and upwards.
 And Mālik said: الطائفة is four.
 Abū Isḥāq said: It is not permissible for a ṭāʾifa to be one, because its meaning is the meaning of a group, and a group cannot be fewer than two, since the meaning of "طائفة" is a portion; one says: "I ate a طائفة of the sheep", that is, a portion of it.
 Yet Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ that they were two men.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: However, what most resembles the meaning of the verse — and Allah knows best — is that the ṭāʾifa in this place be more than one, because what is intended by it is publicity, and this fits a group better.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلزَّانِي لاَ يَنكِحُ إِلاَّ زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَٱلزَّانِيَةُ لاَ يَنكِحُهَآ إِلاَّ زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ وَحُرِّمَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
 Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī and Qatāda said: In the Jāhiliyya there were women known for zinā, and some people among the Muslims wanted to marry them, so the verse came down:
﴿ٱلزَّانِي لاَ يَنكِحُ إِلاَّ زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً﴾. This is the first view.
 And al-Ḥasan said: The flogged adulterer may marry only one like himself.
 Ḥabīb al-Muʿallim said: A man said to ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb: "Al-Ḥasan says such-and-such." He said: "What surprises you about this? Saʿīd ibn Saʿīd al-Maqburī narrated to me from Abū Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The flogged adulterer may marry only one like himself.'"
And Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said something similar.
 And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: النكاح here is sexual intercourse.
 And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The adulterer from the people of the qibla commits zinā only with an adulteress from the people of the qibla or with a polytheist woman; and the adulteress from the people of the qibla commits zinā only with an adulterer from the people of the qibla or with a polytheist man.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: So these are three views.
 And there is a fourth view on the verse which seems to be the most fitting of them.
 Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, known as al-Qaṭṭān, narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Qays al-Anṣārī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: They claim that that verse, ﴿ٱلزَّانِي لاَ يَنكِحُ إِلاَّ زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَٱلزَّانِيَةُ لاَ يَنكِحُهَآ إِلاَّ زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ﴾, was abrogated by the verses after it: ﴿وَأَنْكِحُوْا الأَيَامَى مِنْكُمْ وَالصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وإمَائِكُمْ﴾, so the adulteress came to be included among the unmarried of the Muslims.
We said "this seems more fitting" only because the ḥadīth of al-Qāsim from ʿAbd Allāh has a disturbed (muḍṭarib) chain of transmission «[Translator's note: no ḥadīth of al-Qāsim from ʿAbd Allāh has been cited in this entry as it stands in the source.]», and as for the ḥadīth of Saʿīd from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may have said it before the abrogating verse came down.
 The third view is that النكاح is sexual intercourse; Abū Isḥāq claimed that this is far-fetched, and that النكاح in the sense of intercourse is not known in the Qurʾān; and His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَحُرِّمَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ indicates that it is marriage, because it is not said of zinā that it is forbidden to the believer in particular.
 And the view of whoever said that they were specific known women indicates that this concerned a particular matter which then ceased; so the view of Saʿīd has become the most fitting of them.
Moreover, Saʿīd said "they claim", which indicates that he took it from others, and he would only take it from the Companions.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحُرِّمَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means zinā.

nahhas-meani:4-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُواْ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً وَلاَ تَقْبَلُواْ لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَداً وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ، إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِن بَعْدِ ذٰلِكََ﴾ [verses 4 and 5].
 Abū Jaʿfar said: In this verse there are three rulings against the slanderer (القاذف): among them, flogging him;
not accepting his testimony; and declaring him a sinner (fāsiq).
 And there are three views on it:
 The first, held by al-Ḥasan, Shurayḥ and Ibrāhīm: that the exception is from His saying ﴿وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ﴾; they said: his testimony is not accepted even if he repents; and this is the view of the Kufans.
 The second view: that the exception is from His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلاَ تَقْبَلُواْ لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَداً﴾, that is: except whoever repents, for his testimony is accepted.
 This is the view of Masrūq, ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid and Ṭāwūs.
And it is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said to Abū Bakra: "If you repent, I will accept your testimony"; and this is the view of the people of Medina.
 The third view is related from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The exception is from all three rulings.
So if he repents and his repentance becomes evident, he is not given the ḥadd punishment, his testimony is accepted, and the label of sinfulness is removed from him, because he has become one of those witnesses with whom people are satisfied; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has said: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ وآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صَالِحاًَ ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The exception may be from His saying ﴿وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَاسِقُونَ﴾, as we mentioned in the first view, with ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ in the position of the accusative (naṣb); except that the name of sinfulness must then be removed from him, so his testimony must be accepted and he becomes upright (ʿadl).
 And the exception may be from His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَقْبَلُواْ لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَداً﴾, with ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), in the sense of ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ﴾; then the acceptance of his testimony is more emphatic; and it is also well known from ʿUmar, so it is more fitting for this reason too.
 And it may be as related from al-Shaʿbī, except that the jurists hold the opposite.
 There is an omission in the statement; the meaning is: "and those who accuse chaste women of zinā"; it was omitted because the mention of the fornicatress and the fornicator precedes it.
The point of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَلاَ تَقْبَلُواْ لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَداً﴾ is that ﴿أَبَدَاً﴾ is the extent of the man's lifetime and the extent until his case comes to an end.
 So if you say: "The disbeliever's testimony is never (أبداً) accepted", its meaning is: as long as he remains a disbeliever.
 And if you say: "The slanderer's testimony is never accepted", its meaning is: as long as he remains a slanderer. This is from the side of the language; and the speech of the Arabs confirms the acceptance of his testimony, and that he should not be in a worse state than the killer.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ﴾.
There are two views on this:
 The first: that the meaning is: those who say to their wives "O adulteress", or he says to her "I saw you committing zinā"; this is the view of the people of Kufa.
 The other view: that he says to her "I saw you committing zinā", and nothing else; this is the view of the people of Medina.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting, because the accusing (الرَّمي) in His saying ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المحصَنَاتِ﴾ is that he says to her "O adulteress" or "I saw you committing zinā", so this must be the same.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُمْ شُهَدَآءُ إِلاَّ أَنفُسُهُمْ﴾.
 Ibrāhīm related from ʿAlqama from ʿAbd Allāh that he said: "A man was sitting with us on the eve of Friday, and he said: If one of us finds a man with his wife — if he kills him, you kill him; if he speaks, you give him the ḥadd punishment; and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent in rage. O Allah, judge! Then there was sent down ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُمْ شُهَدَآءُ إِلاَّ أَنفُسُهُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse."
 And Sahl ibn Saʿd said: ʿUwaymir came to the Prophet ﷺ in the midst of the people and asked him — and he mentioned the ḥadīth — and he said at its end: So he divorced her three times.
 And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated the two of them.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْخَامِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعْنَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَاذِبِينَ﴾.
 It is also read "وَالْخَامِسَةََ" [in the accusative], in the sense of: and he bears the fifth testimony.
 And the meaning is: that it is (أنَّه) [i.e. the matter is that] the curse of Allah is upon him; and Sībawayh cited:
في فِتْيةٍ كَسُيوف الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِموُا * أنْ هَالِكٌ كُلُّ مَنْ يَحْفى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like Indian swords, who know that everyone who goes barefoot or shod is perishing.)

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَدْرَؤُاْ عَنْهَا ٱلْعَذَابََ﴾.
 The meaning of ﴿يَدْرأُ﴾ is: it wards off.
There are two views on the meaning of the punishment here:
 The first: that it is imprisonment.
 The other: that it is the ḥadd punishment.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two views on it.
 The first was related by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Let them not swear that they will not benefit anyone.
 The other: that the meaning is: let them not fall short, from their saying مَا أَلَوْتُ أن أفعلَ ("I did not fall short in doing").
Hishām said: And from it is the poet's saying:
أَلاَ رُبَّ خَصْمِ فِيكَ أَلْوى رَدَدْتُهُ * نَصِيحٍ عَلَى تَعْذَالَهِ غَيْرُ مُؤْتَلي
(How many a stubborn adversary concerning you have I repelled — a sincere adviser, unsparing in his reproach.)
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting, because al-Zuhrī related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa, ʿAlqama ibn Waqqāṣ and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: Abū Bakr used to spend on "Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha" because of his kinship and his poverty, and he said: "By Allah, I will not spend on him after what he said about ʿĀʾisha." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤْتُوۤاْ أُوْلِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The grammatical construction (taqdīr) in Arabic is: "and let those of grace not swear, out of aversion to (كراهةَ) giving"; and according to the view of the Kufans: "so that they do not (لأَنْ لا) give".
 And for whoever says its meaning is "let them not fall short", the construction according to him is: "let those of grace not fall short of (عن) giving".
 If it is said: ﴿أُولُو﴾ is for a group, while in the ḥadīth the one intended is Abū Bakr?
 The answer is that ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: Abū Bakr and others of the Muslims said: "We will not do good to anyone of those who spoke about ʿĀʾisha", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ ٱلْغَافِلاَتِ ٱلْمُؤْمِناتِ لُعِنُواْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌٌ﴾.
[Sufyān related from Khuṣayf, who said: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: Is whoever slanders a chaste woman cursed in this world and the Hereafter?] He said: This is specific to ʿĀʾisha.
 And "Salama ibn Nubayṭ" related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: This concerns the wives of the Prophet ﷺ specifically.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk is more fitting than the first view, because His saying ﴿المحصناتِ﴾ indicates a plural. «[Translator's note: no view of Ibn ʿAbbās has been cited in this entry as it stands in the source.]»
 It was also said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ were singled out by this; so of whoever slandered them it was said: "cursed in this world and the Hereafter", while whoever slandered other women was called "a sinner (fāsiq)", and this was not said of him.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾.
الدِّين here means the reckoning and the recompense, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ القَيِّمُ﴾ and ﴿مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَٱلْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَاتِ وَٱلطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَٱلطَّيِّبُونَ لِلْطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾.
 Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid said: That is, the vile words are for the vile among people, and the vile among people are for the vile among speech and the vile among people.
And the good among speech are for the good among people, and the good among people are for the good among speech and the good among people.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best that has been said about this verse.
 The meaning is: vile words are spoken only by vile men and vile women among people, and good words are spoken only by good men and good women among people.
What shows the soundness of this view is: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ﴾, that is, "ʿĀʾisha" and "Ṣafwān" are declared innocent of what the vile men and vile women say.
It is put in the plural even though they were two, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾; this is al-Farrāʾ's view on the plural.
And regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿ٱلْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ﴾ there are two other views:
a- It was said the meaning is: vile speech sticks only to the vile men and vile women among people, not to the good men and good women.
b- And it was said the meaning is: the vile among men are for the vile among women, and the vile among women are for the vile among men.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُواْ وَتُسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا﴾.
 ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: It is only "until you ask permission (تستأذنوا)".
 Mujāhid said: It is clearing the throat and coughing.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: الاستئناس in the language is seeking to find out (الاستعلام); one says: "استأنستُ and I saw no one", as al-Nābigha said:
 كَأَنَّ رَحْلَي وَقَدْ زَالَ النَّهارُ بِنَا * بِذِي الجَلِيلِ عَلَى مُسْتَأْنِسٍ وَحَدِ
(As if my saddle, when the day had declined with us at Dhū al-Jalīl, were upon a solitary [wild bull] on the alert.)
That is, upon a bull that has been startled and is trying to find out about it; and from it is the poet's saying:
آنَسَتْ نَبْأَةً وَأَفْزَعَهَا القَنَّا * صُ عَصْراً وَقَدْ دَنَا الإِمْسَاءُ
(She perceived a faint sound, and the hunters frightened her in the late afternoon, as evening drew near.)
And from it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ رُشْدَاً﴾, that is: if you come to know.
 The marfūʿ ḥadīth (traced back to the Prophet) makes this clear to you.
Abū Burda related from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī that he said: (I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to ask permission to enter, and I said: "Peace be upon you; may we enter?" three times, and I was not given permission. He said: "Why did you not stay?" I said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Let the Muslim man ask permission of his brother three times; if he is given permission [he enters], otherwise he goes back.'" He said: "You will bring me someone to testify for you to this, or a punishment from me will befall you!" So I went to "Ubayy ibn Kaʿb", and he came and testified for me.)
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This makes clear to you that the meaning of ﴿حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا﴾ is: until you find out whether permission is given to you or not.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَجِدُواْ فِيهَآ أَحَداً فَلاَ تَدْخُلُوهَا حَتَّىٰ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾.
 The meaning is: until its owners give you permission to enter, because one ought not to enter another's dwelling — even if he knows that he is not in it — until its owner gives him permission.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ فِيهَا مَتَاعٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: There were houses along the roads of Medina in which people placed their goods, so it was made lawful for them to enter them without permission.
 And Sālim al-Makkī related from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya that he said: They are the rooms of the inns (الخانات) and the market.
 And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the inns.
 And Jābir ibn Zayd said: By المتاع He does not mean equipment; rather it is a house he looks at, or a ruin he enters to relieve himself; and every enjoyment of this world is a benefit.
 And ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿فِيهَا مَتَاعٌ لَكُمْ﴾: for relieving oneself and urinating.
 These views are close to one another, and the clearest of them is Mujāhid's view, because He, the Exalted, first forbade them to enter houses other than their own, then permitted them to enter when they had goods in others' houses, by way of hire or the like.
 What others than Mujāhid said is permissible in the language, because every benefit is called متاع; and from it is ﴿فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى المُوْسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلى الْمُقْتِر قَدَرُهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمْ﴾.
 Qatāda said: That is, from what is not lawful for them.
"مِنْ" here is for specifying the genus (bayān al-jins).
 Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the sudden glance, and he said: Turn your gaze away."
So he ﷺ commanded him to turn his gaze away, because if he did not turn his gaze away he would be abandoning what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded him, and he would be looking a second look by choice, as Abū Salama related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (O ʿAlī, you have a treasure in Paradise, and you are the possessor of its two horns; so do not follow a glance with another glance, for the first is yours, but the last is not yours.)

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلاَّ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا﴾.
 Abū Isḥāq related from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ from ʿAbd Allāh that he said: The earring, the armlet and the bracelet.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا﴾.
There is disagreement about this.
 Abū al-Aḥwaṣ related from ʿAbd Allāh that he said: The clothes.
And this is the position of Abū ʿUbayd.
 And Nāfiʿ related from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: The face and the two hands.
 And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The face and the hand.
 And some of them say from Ibn ʿAbbās: The kohl and the dye (henna); and Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ said the same.
The meaning of kohl and dye and the meaning of the face and the hand are the same.
 And Umm Shabīb related from ʿĀʾisha that she said: The bangle (القُلْب) and the فَتَخَة.
الفَتَخَة is the ring, and its plural is فَتَخ and فَتَخَات.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is close to the view of Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is closer to the meaning of the verse than "clothes", because it is of the same kind as the first adornment.
 Most of the jurists hold it; do you not see that a woman must cover in prayer every part of her that a man may see, and that nothing of her shows except her face and her two hands?!
And القُلْب is the bracelet; Yaḥyā ibn Salmān al-Juʿfī said that.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ نِسَائِهِنَّ﴾.
He means Muslim women.
It is not permissible for them to show that to polytheist women, because of His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿أَوْ نِسَائِهِنَّ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ﴾.
 There are several views on it:
 The first: that they may show that to their male slaves, and that these may see their hair; this view is well known as the view of ʿĀʾisha and Umm Salama.
The two of them treated the slave as a maḥram (unmarriageable relative) in this, because it is not lawful for him to marry his mistress so long as he is owned by her, just as that is not lawful for unmarriageable relatives.
 This is strengthened by His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿ لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ ملكَتْ أيمانُكُم، والَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الحُلُمَ منكُمْ﴾.
 The second view: that their male slaves may not see of them anything except what a stranger may see.
As ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Her slave may not look at her hair or her upper chest; and as for the anklet, none but the husband may look at it.
 This is the position of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Shaʿbī.
 Abū Mālik related from Ibn ʿAbbās the opposite of this; he said: The slave may look at his mistress's hair. And the taqdīr (implied construction) according to the second view is: ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنََّ﴾ who are without desire, or the followers who are without desire; then it was omitted, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بِمَا عنْدَنَا وأنْتَ بِمَا * عِنْدَكَ رَاضٍ وَالرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)
Moreover, Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and ʿĀṣim read ﴿غَيْرَ أُوْلي الإِرْبَةِ﴾ with غير in the accusative; on this basis the exception may apply to both of them together.
The third view: that ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنََّ﴾ refers to slave-women specifically; Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said that; and it was said: the young ones specifically.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is far-fetched in the language, because "ما" is general.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوِ ٱلتَّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي ٱلإِرْبَةِِ﴾.
 ʿAṭāʾ said: He is the one who follows you about and whose concern is his belly.
 ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He is the simpleton; and it was said: the child.
 And al-Shaʿbī said: He is the one who has no desire (أَرَب) for women.
 And ʿIkrima said: He is the impotent man.
 These views are close to one another: he is the one who has no need for women, such as the decrepit old man, the hermaphrodite, the feeble-minded, the child and the impotent.
الإِرْبَة and الأَرَب mean need; and from it is the ḥadīth (And which of you has more control over his desire (لأَرَبه) than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?); whoever relates it "لإِرْبه" has erred, because one says "I cut it إِرْباً إرْباً", that is, limb by limb.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوِ ٱلطِّفْلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَاتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾.
الطِّفل here means children; this is indicated by His saying ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَاتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾, that is, they were not capable of that, as you say: "ظَهَر so-and-so over so-and-so", that is, he overcame him and was strong enough for him.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ﴾.
 Abū al-Jawzāʾ said: They used to strike with their feet so that their anklets would show.
 And Abū Mālik said: They used to put beads on their feet and move them so that the sound would be heard.
 Others said: So they were forbidden that, because it stirs desire.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْكِحُواْ ٱلأَيَامَىٰ مِنْكُمْ وَٱلصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمائِكُمْ﴾.
 Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the women who have no husbands; one says: a أيِّم man, and a أَيِّم woman, and آمَتْ، تَئِيمُ (she has become / becomes unmarried).
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿وَالصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عَبِيدِكُمْ﴾; one says: عَبْد, with the plurals عِبَاد and عَبِيد.
 And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
And likewise His saying ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفرَّقَا يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلاً مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾, that is, through marriage, because He did not make every spouse confined to one spouse forever.
And الفقر is need of the thing mentioned right after it; similar to it is ﴿إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَاءِ﴾, that is, for those in need of the alms; and a man may be in need (فقير) of something without being destitute (مسكين).

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْراًً﴾.
 It was said: This is by way of urging and recommendation, not by way of binding obligation; and were it not for the permission, we would not have known that it is allowed.
كِتَاب and مُكَاتَبة have one meaning (a contract of manumission), just as one says قِتَال and مُقَاتَلة.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: There is disagreement about this.
 Al-Ḥasan said: That is, religion and trustworthiness.
 And Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: That is, truthfulness and fidelity.
 And ʿUbayda said: If they establish the prayer.
 And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: If you know that they intend good by it.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The most comprehensive of them is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, because if he intends good by it he will practise fidelity, as do the people of religion and fidelity, truthfulness and trustworthiness, and whoever establishes the prayer and recognises its due.
 There is another view on the verse.
 Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ said: الخير here is wealth.
This is very far-fetched, because on this view He should have said: "if you know them to have (لهم) good".
 Moreover, the slave is himself property of his master, so how can it be said: "if you know them to have wealth"?
 And Ashhab said: Mālik was asked about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً﴾, and he said: "الخير" is said to be strength and ability to pay.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view: that is, strength to work at a trade and earn, fidelity to what he has made binding on himself, and truthfulness of speech. As for wealth, even though it is a kind of good, it is not in the slave; rather it would be with him or belong to him.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتُوهُمْ مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيۤ آتَاكُمْ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: There are three views on this:
 The first: that it is by way of urging and recommendation.
As Ibn Burayda related from his father, who said: He urged them to this.
This is related from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and al-Zubayr, and from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.
 And the meaning is: give them what will help them pay off the kitāba, by paying to them or by remitting from them.
 The second view: that the master (المكاتِب) remits a fixed amount for his mukātab slave.
 It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said: a quarter; and Mujāhid said likewise.
 And from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: a third.
 The third view was held by Saʿīd ibn Jubayr; he said: He remits for him something of his kitāba; and they did not fix it.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: It was said: the most fitting of them is the first view, because of the eminence of those who held it.
 Moreover, His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَآتُوهُمْ مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيۤ آتَاكُمْ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His saying ﴿فَكَاتِبوهُمْ﴾, so in Arabic it must be like it, by way of urging and recommendation.
 Moreover, the saying of "ʿAlī", peace be upon him, "a quarter", and the saying of ʿAbd Allāh, "a third", do not make it a binding obligation; it may be by way of recommendation.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُكْرِهُواْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: It came down concerning "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl": he ordered his slave-girl to commit zinā, and she brought him a cloak (burd); then he ordered her to return to zinā and she refused, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَلاَ تُكْرِهُواْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ﴾.
And Abū Sufyān related from Jābir, and ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: It came down concerning "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy": he forced his slave-girl into zinā, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَلاَ تُكْرِهُواْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ﴾.
And the question is asked about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّناً﴾.
 The answer is that the meaning is: do not force your slave-girls into prostitution at all.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّناً﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿وَأَنْكِحُوا الأَيَامَى منكُمْ.. إنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنَاً﴾.
 And the meaning of His saying ﴿لِّتَبْتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ is: so that you seek their wages from what they earn.
 And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَن يُكْرِههُنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِن بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: Then Allah, to the women who were forced, after their being forced, is Forgiving, Merciful.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ آيَاتٍ مُّبَيِّنَاتٍٍ﴾.
 Qatāda said: He means the Qurʾān, in which there is the clarification of the lawful from the unlawful.
It is also read "مُبَيِّنَاتٍ" with kasra on the yāʾ, that is, clear and guiding.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is a likeness (tamthīl), that is: by His light the people of the heavens and the earth are guided.
 The implied construction (taqdīr) is: Allah is the Possessor of the light of the heavens and the earth.
And guidance is likened to light.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾: he said: the Guide of the people of the people «[Translator's note: the word "people" (أهل) is repeated in the source.]» of the heavens and the earth; just as His guidance in the heart of the believer is as the pure oil almost gives light before fire touches it, and when it touches it, it increases in light upon light — so is the believer's heart: it acts on guidance before knowledge comes to it, and when knowledge comes to it, it increases in guidance, light upon light.
As Ibrāhīm, may Allah bless him and his family, said — before knowledge came to him, when he saw the star —: ﴿هَذَا رَبِّي﴾, without anyone having told him that he had a Lord; and when Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, told him that He was his Lord, he increased in guidance upon his guidance.
 Ibn ʿAbbās said: This is for the believer.
 And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, the likeness of the believer's light.
 And Abū al-ʿĀliya related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read ﴿مَثَلُ نُورِ المُؤْمِنِ﴾.
 And Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿مَثَلُ نُوْرِهِ﴾: He means the Qurʾān.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning may be: the likeness of His light for the believer, and that is the meaning of Ibn ʿAbbās's saying "for the believer".
And its meaning may be: the likeness of the believer's light is as a niche.
 Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar said: المشكاة is the niche in the wall (الكُوَّة).
 And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb related regarding His saying ﴿لا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلاَ غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾: that is, the sun strikes it at the time of sunrise, so it is eastern and western.
 And ʿIkrima said: It is never without sun at the time of sunrise and sunset, and that makes its oil purer.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيۤءُ﴾, that is, because of its purity, ﴿وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ﴾ — the statement is complete here.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, faith and deeds.
 And others said: the light of the lamp upon the light of the oil and the lantern.
 And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: Its likeness is the likeness of a tree around which other trees are entwined, so the sun does not strike it at any time, and it is green and tender; so is the believer: light upon light — his speech is light, his knowledge is light, and his destination is to light on the Day of Resurrection.
 And al-Suddī said: The light of the fire and the light of the oil: neither one is altered by the alteration of its companion; and so are the light of the Qurʾān and the light of faith.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ﴾.
 The meaning is: as a niche in houses.
 And it was said the meaning is: the lamp is in houses.
 And it was said the meaning is: men glorify Him in houses.
 Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿في بُيُوتٍ﴾, that is, mosques, ﴿أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ﴾, that is, to be revered and protected.
 And ʿIkrima said: They are all houses.
 And Mujāhid said: ﴿أَنْ تُرْفَعَ﴾, that is, to be built.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ. رِجَالٌ لاَّ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلاَ بَيْعٌ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
 ʿAṭāʾ said: That is, neither trade nor selling distracts them from attending the prayer in congregation.
 And Sālim said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar passed through the market when they had closed their shops and stood up to pray in congregation, and he said: Concerning them came down ﴿رِجَالٌ لاَّ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلاَ بَيْعٌ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِقَامِ ٱلصَّلاَةِ وَإِيتَآءِ ٱلزَّكَـاةِ﴾.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخَافُونَ يَوْماً تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾.
That is, the hearts will know the matter by direct sight, and so turn away from the doubt and disbelief they were in, and the believers will increase in certainty; and the covering will be removed from the eyes so that they see; similar to it is ﴿فَكَشَفْنَا عَنْكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ اليَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave a likeness of the disbeliever's deeds — after the believer — and said:
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَسَرَابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ﴾.
 Al-Farrāʾ said: قِيعَة is the plural of قَاع, as one says جِيرَة and جَار.
 And Abū ʿUbayda said: قِيعَة and قَاع are one [i.e. singular].
القَاع and القِيعَة according to the lexicographers are level, open ground in which there is no vegetation.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمْآنُ مَآءً﴾.
That is, the thirsty one; and السَّرَاب (the mirage) is what rises at midday; when it is seen from afar it is thought to be water.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is, when he comes to the place where the mirage is, he does not find it to be anything of what he had supposed, and he finds land with no water in it.
 There is an omission in the statement: so likewise is the likeness of the disbeliever: he imagines that his deeds will benefit him, ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَهُ﴾, that is, [when] he dies, he does not find his deeds to be anything, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has effaced them and nullified them because of his disbelief; ﴿وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُ﴾, that is, at his deeds, ﴿فَوَفَّاهُ حِسَابَهُ﴾, that is, his recompense.
So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, likened the disbeliever's deeds to something that is found [i.e. sought], then likened it to something that is seen, and said:
﴿أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ﴾.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ﴾.
It is a relative adjective (nisba) from اللُّجّ, which is the middle of the sea.
 Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: The disbeliever — his speech is darkness, his deeds are darkness, and his destination is to darkness.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا﴾.
 Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, he did not see it; and ﴿لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا﴾ means: he sees it only with difficulty.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of the views on this is that the meaning is: he did not come near to seeing it; and if he did not come near to seeing it, then he did not see it at all, neither with difficulty nor easily.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلطَّيْرُ صَآفَّاتٍ كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاَتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ﴾.
 Al-Firyābī narrated to us: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba informed us: Shabāba informed us, from Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاَتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ﴾: Prayer is for the human being, and glorification (التسبيح) is for the rest of His creation.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحَاباًً﴾.
That is, He drives it; ﴿ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ﴾, that is, He gathers the scattered pieces until they join together; ﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكَاماً﴾, that is, piled one on another; ﴿فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ﴾.
الوَدْق is rain; one says وَدَقَتْ سُرَّتُه تَدِقُ وَدْقاً وَدِقَةً (his navel oozed), and everything that issues forth is وَادِق, as the poet said:
فَلاَ مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها * وَلاَ أَرْضَ أبْقَلَ إِبْقَالَهَا
(No rain-cloud ever poured down rain like hers, and no land ever brought forth herbage like hers.)
And "خِلاَل" is the plural of خَلَل (gap), as one says جَبَل and جِبَال.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾.
 It was said: the meaning is "from mountains of hail in it", as you say "this is a ring in my hand of iron", that is, "this is an iron ring in my hand".
 Just as one says "mountains of clay" and "clay mountains".
 And it was said: the meaning is "from the amount of mountains", then [the word "amount"] was omitted, as you say "so-and-so has mountains of wealth".
 And al-Akhfash holds that "مِنْ" in both of them is redundant (zāʾida), that is: mountains in which there is hail.
 He said: And some of them said: the mountains are of hail ﴿فِيهَا﴾, [i.e.] in the sky, and you make the sending down from them.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾.
That is, the brightness of its lightning.
 And Rabīʿa ibn Abyaḍ related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Lightning is the angels' whips (مخاريق)."
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: It is what comes from the mountains of hail.
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Kātib narrated to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated to me: my father narrated to me: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, that he read ﴿يَكَادُ سَنَاءُ بُرَقِهِ﴾.
 Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: It is the plural of بُرْقَة.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: البُرْقَة is a quantity of lightning, and البَرْقَة is a single flash, like غُرْفة (a handful) and غَرْفَة (a single scoop).

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍ مِّن مَّآءٍٍ﴾.
 Every animal, whether rational or not, is called دابّة.
 Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَمْشِي عَلَىٰ بَطْنِهِ﴾.
He did not say "فمنها" or "فمنهن", because He gave precedence to the rational; and since the pronoun referred to what is used for the rational, He brought "مَنْ" and did not bring "ما". Do you not see that He mixed, at the beginning of the statement, the rational with the non-rational?!

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن يَكُنْ لَّهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ يَأْتُوۤاْ إِلَيْهِ مُذْعِنِينََ﴾.
 ʿAṭāʾ said: That is, hastening; and they are Quraysh. One says أذعن when someone comes hastening, obedient, not compelled.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَخَافُونَ أَن يَحِيفَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾.
 The meaning is: or do they fear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will be unjust to them?
 And His saying ﴿أَمْ يَخَافُونَ أَن يَحِيفَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ is an opening of speech; do you not see that before it is ﴿وَإِذَا دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, and He did not say "ليحكما بينهم" (that the two may judge between them)?!
 This is as one says: "Allah has freed you, and I have freed you", and "What Allah wills, then what you will."

nahhas-meani:51-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوْلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذَا دُعُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْْ﴾.
A statement of fact (khabar) carrying the meaning of command and urging.
That is, they ought only to be like this.
 It was read before Bakr ibn Sahl, from ʿAmr ibn Hishām — that is, al-Bayrūtī — from Ibn Abī Karīma, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَخْشَ ٱللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُون﴾.
 He said: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ and so affirms His oneness, ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ and so believes him, ﴿وَيَخْشَ ٱللَّهَ﴾ regarding his past sins, ﴿وَيَتَّقْهِ﴾ in what remains of his life, ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُون﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: الفوز in the language is deliverance.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ قُل لاَّ تُقْسِمُواْ﴾.
 ﴿قُلْ لا تُقْسِمُوْا﴾ — the statement is complete; then He said ﴿طَاعَةٌ مَعْرُوْفَةٌ﴾, that is, a known [i.e. sincere] obedience is better; and this is addressed to the hypocrites.
That is, do not swear to a lie, for obedience is better.
 And the meaning may be: let there be obedience from you.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ مَا حُمِّلَ وَعَلَيْكُمْ مَّا حُمِّلْتُمْ﴾.
 The meaning is "فإن تتولوا" (if you turn away), then [one tāʾ] was omitted; this is indicated by the fact that after it is ﴿وَعَلَيْكُمْ مَّا حُمِّلْتُمْ﴾, and He did not say "وعليهم".
 The meaning is: upon the Prophet ﷺ is only the conveying, and upon you is the accepting; it is not his responsibility that you accept.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
He brought the lām [of the oath], because the meaning of "وَعَدَ" and "قَالَ" is the same.
The meaning is: He will surely make them succeed those before them.
﴿وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ﴾, and that is Islam.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مُعْجِزِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, they are in the grip of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسْتَأْذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ﴾.
 There are several views on this verse:
a- Ibn Jurayḥ «[Translator's note: so written in the source (ابن جريح); presumably Ibn Jurayj.]» related from Mujāhid that he said: They are the owned male slaves.
2- And Isrāʾīl related from Layth from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar: ﴿لِيَسْتَأْذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ﴾: the females.
3- And Sufyān related from Abū Ḥuṣayn from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that he said: It is for women specifically.
That is, the way of men is to ask permission at every time, while women ask permission at these times specifically.
 It is not permissible in the language to say "الَّذِينَ" of women; had it been for women specifically, it would have been "اللاَّتِي" or "اللاَّئِي" or the like — unless masculine and feminine are combined, in which case "الَّذِينَ" is said of them all.
 And ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr related from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that two men from the people of Iraq asked him about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لِيَسْتَأْذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ﴾, and he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is One who conceals and loves concealment. The Muslims at that time had no curtains or canopied alcoves, so a man's child, his servant and his orphan would sometimes come in on him while he was with his wife; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded asking permission. Then when Allah expanded provision, and people took curtains and alcoves, they considered that this made asking permission unnecessary for them" — and in some narrations: "so people abandoned acting on the verse."
 Al-Shaʿbī said: It is not abrogated.
 The most fitting thing on this, and the soundest in chain of transmission, is what ʿAbd al-Malik related from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: There are three verses which people have abandoned acting upon:
a- His saying ﴿لِيَسْتَأْذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْْ﴾.
b- And His saying ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ ﴾.
And so-and-so says: "I am nobler than so-and-so", whereas the nobler of the two is only the more God-fearing of them.
 ʿAṭāʾ said: And I forgot the third.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is from Ibn ʿAbbās by way of disapproval, and it explains what ʿIkrima related, in the narration of whoever said: "so people abandoned acting on it."
 And Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "I indeed command this slave-girl of mine — and he pointed to a short, fair slave-girl — to ask permission to come in to me."
 Then He clarified the times, saying, Glorified is He: ﴿مِّن قَبْلِ صَـلَوٰةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾, because it is the time in which people put on their clothes, coming out of their beds;
﴿وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَـٰبَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ﴾, because it is the time of the midday nap;
﴿وَمِن بَعْدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْعِشَآءِ﴾: al-Zuhrī said: and it is what people call al-ʿatama.
 He said: So they ask permission at these times specifically; as for others, they ask permission at every time.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ لَّكُمْ﴾.
 That is, the times of asking permission are three times of privacy.
And the accusative reading has the sense of: they ask permission at the time of three times of privacy for you.
﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلاَ عَلَيْهِمْ جُنَاحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ﴾, that is, in entering without permission.
 ﴿طَوَٰفُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, that is, they serve you.
 ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾, that is, some of you go about among others.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلأَطْفَالُ مِنكُمُ ٱلْحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُواْ﴾.
 Al-Zuhrī said: That is, a man asks permission to come in to his mother; and it was concerning this meaning that this verse came down.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿كَمَا ٱسْتَأْذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
He means those who have reached maturity.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْقَوَاعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّلاَتِي لاَ يَرْجُونَ نِكَاحاًً﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: those who have ceased bearing children.
 And others said: What is meant by this is the very old woman who has ceased moving about, because she may cease bearing children while there is still something left in her.
 Rabīʿa said: She is the one whom, when you see her, you find unappealing.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ﴾.
 Abū Wāʾil related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: He means the outer cloak (الرِّداء).
 Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known of the reading of ʿAbd Allāh is ﴿أَنْ يَضَعْنَ مِنْ ثِيابِهِنَّ﴾.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَن يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُنَّ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, that they wear the outer garment (الجلباب) is better for them.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾.
 Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us: Zayd ibn Ajzam narrated to us: Bishr ibn ʿUmar al-Zahrānī informed us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: The Muslims used to go out all together (يُوْعبون) on campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they would hand their keys to their disabled ones (ضَمْناهم) and say: "If you are in need, eat." But they would say: "They only made it lawful for us without real goodwill." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكُم جناح أَن تَأْكُلُواْ﴾ ﴿مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبَآئِكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: "يوعبون" means: they go out, all of them, on the military expeditions.
One says: "Banū so-and-so أوعبَ against Banū so-and-so" when they come at them all together; and one says "a وَعِيب house" when it is spacious, taking in (يستوعب) everything put into it.
 And الضَّمْنَى are the chronically disabled (الزَّمْنى); the singular is ضَمِن, like زَمِن.
 Maʿmar said: I asked al-Zuhrī about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾: why are these mentioned here? He said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that when people went out on campaign, they would hand their keys to the disabled and make it lawful for them to eat from what was in their houses; but they would not do so, being wary and saying: "They only gave us leave without real goodwill." So Allah sent down the verse ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this view is clear: that is, there is nothing against them in eating.
 The other view is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; Bakr ibn Sahl narrated it to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَأْكُلُواْ﴾ ﴿مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿جَمِيعاً أَوْ أَشْتَاتاً﴾: that was when Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالبَاطِلِ﴾, and the Muslims said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has forbidden us to consume our wealth among ourselves wrongfully, and food is among the best of wealth, so it is not lawful for any of us to eat at anyone else's." So people refrained from that; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down after that ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ﴾ up to His saying ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَّفَاتِحهُ﴾ — that is the man who entrusts a man with his estate.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: What Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, permitted to be eaten of that is food and dates, and drinking milk. They were also wary and scrupled that a man should eat food alone without someone else being with him, so Allah gave them leave and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَأْكُلُواْ جَمِيعاً أَوْ أَشْتَاتاً﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: So Ibn ʿAbbās made clear in this ḥadīth what food they were given leave to take.
 And in another narration from him: the blind man used to scruple about eating another's food because he might put his hand in the wrong place, the lame man scrupled because he took up much room in the place, and the sick man because of his smell and what affected him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, permitted them to eat with others.
 This is the meaning of Ṣāliḥ's narration from him.
 As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَن تَأْكُلُواْ مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ [verse 61].
 It was said its meaning is: from the houses of your dependants.
 And it was said its meaning is: from the houses of your children, because their children are of their earning, so their houses were attributed «[Translator's note: the source has فنسيت ("were forgotten"); the sense requires فنُسبت ("were attributed"), which is translated here.]» to them.
 The proponent of this view argued that He mentioned the relatives afterwards but did not mention the children.
The meaning of "إخوانكم" and "إخوتكم" is the same.
 And in a narration from Ibn ʿAbbās other than that of Muʿāwiya: ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَّفَاتِحهُ﴾ means: the slaves.
 And it was said: He means the disabled: they were permitted what they had stored of this for the campaigners.
 And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read ﴿أَوْ مَا مُلّكْتُمْ مَفَاتِحَهُ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and a doubled lām.
 And Mujāhid said: A man would take the blind, the lame and the sick to his father's house or that of another relative, and he would scruple about that, saying: "It is someone else's house"; so this verse came down as a concession.
 And it was said: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ﴾, that is, in [staying away from] the campaign, and likewise the lame and the sick.
 ﴿وَلاَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَن تَأْكُلُواْ مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾.
That is, from your own houses, because it would have been possible for that to be forbidden, since in a man's house there may be what does not belong to him.
 And it would have been possible for another's property to be forbidden to him even if he were given permission; so that was made permissible for this reason, when one of these gives him permission.
And both the specific and the general were mentioned among them, because His saying ﴿أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوَانِكُمْ﴾ is general.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتاً فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
 ʿAmr ibn Dīnār related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتَاً﴾: he said: the mosques;
﴿فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾: he says: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah."
 And Abū Mālik said: When you enter houses in which there is none of the Muslims, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah."
 And Māhān said: When you enter a house in which there is no one, say: "Peace be upon us from our Lord."
 And al-Ḥasan said: ﴿فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾: let some of you greet others with peace,
as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
 Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Greet your families and others with peace.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Ḥasan's view on this is a sound view in the language; the Muslim, in relation to the Muslim, is like his own self, because their religion is one and each of them owes his companion sincere counsel; and the poet said:
 * "قد جعلتُ نفسي في الأديم" *
(I have put my very self into the leather skin.)
He means the water: because life depends on water, he made it his self; likewise the Muslim feels at ease with the Muslim as he feels at ease with himself.
 What is more fitting is that it applies to all houses, because the wording is general; and the meaning is: let some of you greet others, a greeting from Allah, blessed and good.
 Then He reported that the greeting of peace is good and blessed, saying ﴿تَحِيَّةً مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُبَارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً﴾.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ جَامِعٍ لَّمْ يَذْهَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ﴾.
 Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: When some matter of war or the like befell them, they asked his permission before leaving.
 And Mujāhid said: This is in campaigns and on Friday.
 And Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ جَامِعٍ﴾, that is, on a matter of obedience.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is the most fitting of them: that is, when the imam needs to gather the Muslims for a matter requiring their assembly, the imam has the choice to give leave to whomever he sees fit to give leave.
As for when one's ablution is broken on Friday, there is no reason for him to stay in the mosque, and no sense in his asking the imam's permission for that, because it is not permissible for him to prevent him.
 And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ﴾.
 Qatāda said: He, Glorified is He, had said ﴿عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ﴾, so this one — meaning the one in Sūrat al-Nūr — abrogated the one in Sūrat Barāʾa.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ تَجْعَلُواْ دُعَآءَ ٱلرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعَآءِ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضاًً﴾.
 Mujāhid said: Say "O Messenger of Allah" gently and softly, and do not say "O Muḥammad" with a frown.
 And Qatāda said: They were commanded to venerate and honour him.
 And it is related that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger's supplication against you is answered, so beware of it.
 This is a good view, because the discourse is connected: what precedes it and what follows it is a prohibition against opposing him; that is, do not expose yourselves to what angers him, lest he supplicate against you and you perish; and do not treat his supplication like the supplication of other people.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمْ لِوَاذاً﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, in opposition.
 And it was said: turning aside, as you say "لُذْتُ من فلانٍ", that is, I turned aside from him.
 And it was said: ﴿لِوَاذَاً﴾ means under cover; and "لُذْتُ من فلان" means I withdrew from him under cover.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another.
 Mujāhid's view is indicated by ﴿فَلْيَحْذَرِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُخَالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾.
 And ﴿لِوَاذٌ﴾ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "لاَوَذَ"; as for "لاَذَ", its maṣdar is لِيَاذ.
 And Abū ʿUbayda claimed that His saying ﴿فَلْيَحْذَرِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُخَالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾
means: they oppose His command (يخالفون أمره).
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is mistaken according to the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because that is not done with "عَنْ" and "عَلَى", that is, they are not made redundant; and "عَنْ" in its place is not redundant.
 The meaning is: they act contrary after He has commanded, as the poet said:
 * "نَؤُوْمُ الضُحَّى لم تَنْتَطِقْ عَنْ تَفَضُّل" *
(She sleeps late into the forenoon, and has not girded herself after [wearing] a loose house-garment.)
And the true sense of "عن" here, if you wish: their acting contrary [comes] after His commanding, so their contrariness is away from (عن) His command. This is the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; they said the same about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾.
